## 2. Replica layouts: drift invariants

Every SQL snapshot that has a `customer_data_primary` table plus replicas, including the sample-truth read replicas, so the three eval-only layouts can be compared with the ones the samples exercise.

| file | family | topology | tables | rows | rows only in a replica | what kind | primary vs replica content differs | rows dated after the snapshot | eval-only layout |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| evidence_05 | data:read_replica | read_replica | 2 | 61 | 1 | customer_profiles | 0 | 0 | no |
| evidence_10 | data:read_replica | read_replica | 2 | 59 | 1 | customer_profiles | 0 | 0 | no |
| evidence_15 | data:read_replica | read_replica | 2 | 49 | 1 | customer_profiles | 0 | 0 | no |
| evidence_20 | data:read_replica | read_replica | 2 | 63 | 1 | customer_profiles | 0 | 0 | no |
| evidence_24 | data:read_replica | read_replica | 2 | 50 | 2 | customer_profiles | 0 | 0 | no |
| evidence_29 | data:regional_replicas | regional_replicas | 3 | 85 | 1 | customer_profiles | 0 | 0 | yes |
| evidence_33 | data:regional_replicas | regional_replicas | 3 | 89 | 2 | customer_profiles | 0 | 0 | yes |
| evidence_38 | data:regional_replicas | regional_replicas | 3 | 85 | 1 | customer_profiles | 0 | 0 | yes |
| evidence_43 | data:reporting_replica | reporting_replica | 2 | 51 | 1 | customer_profiles | 0 | 0 | yes |
| evidence_47 | data:reporting_replica | reporting_replica | 2 | 49 | 1 | customer_profiles | 0 | 0 | yes |
| evidence_52 | data:failover_replica | failover_replica | 2 | 32 | 0 | - | 0 | 0 | yes |

Invariants over 11 files: ghost kinds {'customer_profiles': 10}; primary/replica content differences 0; rows dated after their snapshot 0. So replication drift always means the same thing in every layout: an account profile that exists only in a replica. That is why generic SQL rows are stamped with the snapshot time rather than their own `updated_at` (never later).

Ghost accounts checked end to end: 12 replica-only rows; 12 (ghost, case) pairs where the owner has a case within 14 days after the snapshot; the pipeline reports the ghost as a remaining record in **12/12**.


## 3. Cross-format consistency

The same resource read through two different files, observation times within one hour: do the two formats give the same record type and state? Pairs are grouped by the formats involved.

| format pair | agree | differ |
|---|---|---|
| bundle / inventory_sql | 43 | 2 |
| bundle / log | 26 | 0 |
| bundle / readback_json | 29 | 2 |
| bundle_ledger / inventory_sql | 21 | 0 |
| bundle_ledger / log | 16 | 0 |
| inventory_sql / log | 40 | 1 |
| log / log | 12 | 1 |
| log / readback_json | 17 | 0 |

Overall: 204 agree, 6 differ.

- differs (bundle / inventory_sql): support_2315: evidence_12 says SUPPORT_ATTACHMENT/PRESENT, evidence_87 says SUPPORT_MESSAGE/EXPOSED
- differs (bundle / inventory_sql): support_2283: evidence_17 says SUPPORT_ATTACHMENT/PRESENT, evidence_84 says SUPPORT_MESSAGE/EXPOSED
- differs (bundle / readback_json): support_3684: evidence_26 says SUPPORT_ATTACHMENT/PRESENT, evidence_77 says SUPPORT_MESSAGE/EXPOSED
- differs (bundle / readback_json): support_3615: evidence_40 says SUPPORT_ATTACHMENT/PRESENT, evidence_68 says SUPPORT_MESSAGE/EXPOSED
- differs (inventory_sql / log): support_1370: evidence_06 says SUPPORT_ATTACHMENT/PRESENT, evidence_93 says SUPPORT_MESSAGE/EXPOSED
- differs (log / log): support_9309: evidence_11 says SUPPORT_ATTACHMENT/PRESENT, evidence_88 says SUPPORT_MESSAGE/EXPOSED

All the disagreements are one phenomenon: a support id that a home file renders as a ticket with requester details (message) and a later-captured file renders as an attachment. See evaluation_report.md, open risks.
